topics.blurb: The kanji you read off a menu, a shop curtain or a set-meal board. Learn this chapter and you can order without pointing.
topics.foot: 和 and 洋 divide almost everything in Japan: 和食/洋食, 和室/洋室, 和服/洋服.

kanji + kana · 欠ける・かける
rows.story: Food and an open mouth, tipped back.

rows.story: Old grass. Chew it and see.

rows.story: Small, with a bit shaved off.
rows.wild: 少なめ — 'less, please', useful for rice portions

topics.blurb: Bars, music and cinema. Most of these turn up on a poster or a karaoke screen rather than in a textbook.
topics.foot: 楽 has two readings and two lives: 楽しい (fun) and 音楽 (music). Same kanji, same underlying idea of ease.

rows.wild: 夜行バス — the overnight coach

rows.story: The sun making its escape below the roofline.

rows.wild: 音楽 is music; 音 alone is any noise

rows.story: A bent frame with slats in it. A tune is a line that bends.
rows.wild: Karaoke menus list everything by 曲名

rows.story: Sun striking dead centre and bouncing straight back at you.
rows.wild: 映画館 — cinema

parts: kanji + kana · 欠ける・かける
rows.story: Sing until you run out of breath, then sing again.
rows.wild: 歌 alone is the song; 歌手 is the singer

rows.story: Sweeping up and going home.
rows.wild: 終電で帰る — go home on the last train

rows.story: The mouth stretched long to reach someone at a distance.
rows.wild: 呼び出し — calling staff over, or a tannoy page

rows.story: A wooden rattle strung with beads. Shake it and everything gets easier.
rows.wild: 音楽 uses the same kanji: sound that is easy

rows.story: A second-rate heart. Not broken, just not good.
rows.wild: 気分が悪い — feeling ill, which you may need

rows.story: A bow so strong an insect could not bend it.
rows.wild: お酒に強い — holds their drink

rows.story: Two bows with feathers instead of strings.
rows.wild: お酒に弱い — does not

topics.blurb: Shops, prices, parcels and the clothes and objects you carry home. Heavy on verbs, because shopping is mostly transactions.
topics.foot: Notice how many shopping words are pairs of opposites: 売/買, 貸/借, 送/返. Learn them in pairs.

rows.story: The metal that stubbornly refuses to be gold.

rows.story: A person standing in at a marked stake while the real one is away.

rows.story: Money weighed against two axes. What is it actually worth?
rows.wild: 質屋 is a pawn shop, using the older sense

rows.story: Something you keep an eye on, on a table, with legs. A tool.
rows.wild: 家具 is furniture — household tools

rows.story: Grass bundled up and someone asking what on earth is inside it.
rows.wild: On every delivery slip and hotel front desk

rows.story: A hand fitting cloth to a kneeling body.
rows.wild: 制服 is a uniform

rows.story: Water so wide there are sheep on the far side of it. Hence: foreign, Western.
rows.wild: 洋 also means ocean — the far side of it

rows.story: A cow with a banner on it: livestock, and by extension all goods.
rows.wild: 買い物, 食べ物, 荷物 — 物 is everywhere

rows.story: A samurai covering the goods and walking off with the takings.
rows.wild: 売り切れ — sold out, on vending machines

rows.story: Money that has been substituted for a promise.
rows.wild: 貸出中 — currently on loan

rows.story: A person still holding what they took long ago. That is borrowing.
rows.wild: Renting a flat is 借りる, not 買う

rows.story: A hand taking an ear. Grim, historical, and unforgettable.
rows.wild: お取り置き — holding an item for you

rows.story: Putting something on the road with a farewell attached.

rows.story: Movement in reverse. Give it back.

rows.wild: 使用中 — in use, on toilet doors

rows.story: Carrying something all the way to the temple in your hands.
rows.wild: お持ち帰り — takeaway

rows.wild: 売り切れ again: sold through and cut off

rows.story: A cart that goes straight down the road because there is nothing in it.
rows.wild: 軽自動車 — the small-engine car class

rows.story: A load with a person underneath, pressed down.

rows.story: The one cow reserved for the temple.
rows.wild: 特売 — special offer; 特急 — limited express

topics.blurb: The vocabulary you need when something is wrong. Worth learning before you need it rather than after.
topics.foot: Japanese medical signage is unusually kanji-heavy. 内科, 外科, 歯科 on a clinic door tell you which department you want.

parts: radical · a box on its side
rows.story: Arrows kept in a box, ready to be pulled back out of people.
rows.wild: 医院 on a small clinic's sign

rows.story: A walled compound up on a hill. Hospitals and temples both.
rows.wild: 院 alone marks any walled institution

rows.story: Someone laid against the wall, third one this week.
rows.wild: 急病 — sudden illness

parts: kanji + kana · 楽しい・たのしい
rows.story: The plant that makes things easier.
rows.wild: 薬局 — pharmacy; 薬屋 — chemist's shop

rows.story: A person's original issue, the thing they were born holding: the body.
rows.wild: 体調 — physical condition

rows.story: A bean on top of a head. Anatomically fair.
rows.wild: 頭痛 — headache

rows.story: An eye with hair above it and a neck below.
rows.wild: 手首 is wrist, 足首 ankle

rows.story: A hand with the last stroke let loose to curl.
rows.wild: 髪の毛 — the hair on your head

rows.story: The front of the head, and the part people judge.
rows.wild: 洗顔 — face washing, on cosmetics

rows.story: A knee above a foot. Enough leg to get you there — hence also 'sufficient'.
rows.wild: 足りる, from the same kanji, means 'to suffice'

rows.story: A heart with three drops flying off it. Covers the mind as well as the feelings.
rows.wild: 心配 — worry; 安心 — relief

rows.story: A person kneeling beside bones.
rows.wild: Blunt in Japanese too; 亡くなる is the polite form

rows.story: A baby turned the right way up, being fed until it has flesh on it.
rows.wild: 教育 — education

rows.story: Adding your strength to a pile someone else is already carrying.
rows.wild: 助けて! is the shout for help

rows.story: Water first, before anything else happens.
rows.wild: 手を洗いましょう on every washroom sign

rows.story: A heart with a great NO written above it.
rows.wild: 悲鳴 — a scream

rows.story: Measuring with an arrow and finding only a bean's worth.
rows.wild: 短気 — short-tempered

topics.blurb: Stations, roads, timetables and the verbs of movement. The single most useful chapter if you are actually in Japan.
topics.foot: 辶, the sweeping road element, appears in 道 通 進 迎 遅 近 遠 運 送 返 — ten of the movement kanji at this level.

rows.wild: 駅前 — in front of the station, the standard meeting point

rows.story: Your head pointed down a path. The way you are heading is your way.

parts: kanji + kana · 小さい・ちいさい
rows.story: A tall building on a hill with small ones below. A capital city.
rows.wild: 京都 is Kyoto — literally the capital city

rows.story: That particular piece of ground, the one under your feet.
rows.wild: 地下 means underground

rows.story: A plough turning at the end of a furrow: which way it points.
rows.wild: 読み方 — how to read it; also polite for 'person'

rows.story: People setting off in one direction together.
rows.wild: 旅館 — traditional inn

rows.story: Wheels turning over like clouds.
rows.wild: 運転 — driving

rows.story: A hand clutching at your heart. Something needs doing now.
rows.wild: 特急 is faster still; check before boarding

parts: kanji + kana · 与える・あたえる
rows.story: Putting a cover over something and handing on a duplicate.

rows.story: A foot pushing off the earth.

rows.story: A bird on the road, and birds only ever hop forward.

rows.story: Movement through a funnel: in one end, out the other.
rows.wild: 通勤 — commuting

rows.story: Going out onto the road to meet someone coming in.

rows.story: An army on the move. Whether it arrives is partly luck.

rows.story: Within one axe-throw of here.

topics.blurb: Where you live, and what you do there. Short chapter, high daily frequency.

parts: radical · a roof with walls, on top
kanji + kana · 至る・いたる
rows.story: The place under the roof you finally arrive at.
rows.wild: 洋室 is the Western-style alternative

rows.story: A small raised mouth: something to stand on and speak from.
rows.wild: 台 alone is any raised stand or platform

rows.story: A door and an axe: the spot where the work happens.
rows.wild: 住所 — address; 台所, 近所 all use it

rows.story: That particular patch of water, the one that never goes anywhere.
rows.wild: 電池 is a battery — a pond of electricity

parts: kanji + kana · 主に・おもに
rows.story: The person who is master of this address is the one who lives here.
rows.wild: 住所 — where you live

rows.story: A brush drawing plans, stretched out across a plot of ground.
rows.wild: 建物 — a building

parts: kanji + kana · 走る・はしる

parts: radical · building, open on one side
rows.story: A building with the walls taken out.
rows.wild: 広告 — an advertisement, spread wide

rows.story: No sun, only sound. When you can hear but not see, it is dark.
rows.wild: 暗証番号 — your PIN, a 'dark' number

rows.story: Sun and moon in the sky at once — the brightest thing you can draw.
rows.wild: 説明 — explanation, making things bright

topics.foot: 習 and 勉 are not interchangeable: 習う is learning from someone, 勉強する is grinding at it yourself.

rows.story: A person in service to a samurai. The polite verb for doing.
rows.wild: 仕方がない — 'nothing to be done'

rows.story: A hand holding a brush over a record. An affair, a matter.
rows.wild: 用事 — an errand; 大事 — important

rows.story: A rack of wooden tools, all in use. That is an industry.

rows.story: An altar on the earth. Shrines first, then companies.
rows.wild: 社会 reverses it: society

rows.story: One more mouth on the payroll.
rows.wild: 店員, 駅員, 会員 — 員 is anyone on a roster

rows.story: Someone on this earth, under this sun. The generic person suffix.

rows.story: How far up the thread you have reached.
rows.wild: JLPT levels were once called 級

rows.story: A formal set of words you have to get through.

rows.story: Two hands working a stone smooth. Research is the same job.
rows.wild: 研修 — training

rows.story: What the head is supposed to be correct about.
rows.wild: 話題 — a topic of conversation

rows.story: A mouth at the gate. You cannot come in until you have answered.
rows.wild: 問い合わせ — an enquiry

parts: radical · a roof with walls, on top
rows.story: A child under a roof, being made to write.
rows.wild: 文字 — a written character

rows.story: The great river culture. 漢字 are the characters that came down it.
rows.wild: 漢 alone points at the Han dynasty

rows.wild: 手紙 is a letter — hand paper

rows.wild: 文化 — culture; 作文 — composition

rows.story: Words and numbers together. Counting out loud.
rows.wild: 時計 — clock, a thing that counts

rows.story: Words traded until both sides understand.
rows.wild: 小説 — a novel

rows.story: The flower at the very centre. Also the standard kanji for England.
rows.wild: 英国 — the United Kingdom

parts: kanji + kana · 動く・うごく

rows.wild: 労働 — labour

rows.story: Effort spent escaping ignorance. Which is what you are doing now.
rows.wild: 勉強中 — studying right now

rows.story: An old-fashioned picture of instruction. Effective as a memory hook.
rows.wild: 教室 — classroom

parts: kanji + kana · 白い・しろい
rows.story: A fledgling flapping white wings over and over until it can fly.
rows.wild: 練習 — practice

rows.story: An old person with a bent back, taking their time over it.
rows.wild: 考え方 — a way of thinking

rows.story: An answer that leaves the mouth as straight and fast as an arrow. You knew it.
rows.wild: お知らせ — a notice

rows.story: A woman stepping onto the platform. Everything starts here.
rows.wild: 開始 — the start

rows.story: The thread runs out in winter. Nothing comes after.
rows.wild: 終電 — the last train

rows.story: Birds settling into one tree at dusk, all of them at once.
rows.wild: 集合 — assembly, meeting up

parts: kanji + kana · 止まる・とまる
rows.story: Stop precisely on the line. That is correct.
rows.wild: 正解 — the right answer

topics.blurb: Almost all nouns, because relationships are things rather than actions. Note that Japanese uses different words for your own family and someone else's.
topics.foot: Japanese has two sets of family words: humble ones for your own family (兄, 姉, 父) and honorific ones for other people's (お兄さん, お姉さん, お父さん).

rows.story: Standing on a tree to watch your child leave. That is a parent.
rows.wild: 両親 — both parents; 親切 — kind

rows.story: The one with legs and a big mouth, who tells the younger ones what to do.
rows.wild: お兄さん for someone else's

rows.story: A bow with the string wound down it. The one still being wound up.
rows.wild: 弟子 — a disciple

rows.story: The sister old enough to be sent to market.
rows.wild: お姉さん for someone else's

rows.story: The sister who is not yet old enough.
rows.wild: No honorific version in common use

rows.story: Everyone who marches under the same banner in the same direction.
rows.wild: 民族 — an ethnic group

rows.story: A king with a lamp above him. The main one in the room.
rows.wild: ご主人 for someone else's husband

rows.story: An eye with a spike driven through it — the old, brutal picture for a subject population.
rows.wild: 市民 — city residents

rows.story: Not this person — that one over there.
rows.wild: その他 — 'and others', on forms

parts: kanji + kana · 大きい・おおきい
rows.story: A big animal with one ear flicked up.
rows.wild: 犬 with the dot; 大 without

rows.story: A crest, a body, four tail ticks.
rows.wild: 焼き鳥 — grilled chicken skewers

rows.story: Horns lifting off a flat body.
rows.wild: 牛肉 — beef; 牛乳 — milk

topics.blurb: Small chapter, but these are the words you need to agree, disagree, or say what you meant.
topics.foot: 別々にお願いします — 'separately, please' — is the single most useful phrase in this chapter.

rows.story: The sound your heart makes before you say it out loud.
rows.wild: どういう意味? — 'what does that mean?'

rows.story: Words getting heated.
rows.wild: 相談する — to talk something over

rows.story: A mouth with sound waves stacked above it and a lid on top.
rows.wild: 方言 — dialect

rows.story: A heart with a field laid over it: the mind divided into neat plots.
rows.wild: 〜と思います softens almost any opinion

rows.story: One cover, one mouth, everybody underneath saying the same thing.
rows.wild: 同時 — at the same time

rows.story: A sword coming down between two things.
rows.wild: 別々に — separately, when splitting a bill

rows.story: A bird flying up and hitting a ceiling. It does not get through.

topics.blurb: Days, seasons and the adjectives that go with them. Nearly all of these appear on a schedule or a shop's opening hours.

rows.story: Days flying past on wings, one bird after another.
rows.wild: 月曜日 through 日曜日

parts: kanji + kana · 周り・まわり
rows.story: One full lap of the road. Seven days and you are back where you started.
rows.wild: 週末 — weekend

rows.story: The sun already up but the moon still visible. That overlap is morning.
rows.wild: 朝食 — breakfast

rows.story: The sun measured and found to be exactly overhead.
rows.wild: 昼休み — lunch break

rows.story: The moon with one stroke missing — the moon before it has properly come out.
rows.wild: 夕食 — dinner

rows.story: The day that has already been cut away behind you.
rows.wild: An irregular reading; learn the word whole

rows.story: Three people out in the sun for the first time this year.
rows.wild: 春休み — spring holiday

rows.story: Stubble burnt off after the harvest.
rows.wild: 秋分の日 — the autumn equinox holiday

rows.story: That particular run of months. A term.
rows.wild: 学期 — a school term

parts: radical · building, open on one side
rows.story: Measuring a building twenty times over by hand.
rows.wild: 温度 — temperature, also degrees

rows.story: Walking off your own patch of ground. Once you have, it is the past.
rows.wild: 過去 — the past

rows.story: The sun already ten strokes above the horizon and you are still in bed.
rows.wild: 早く! — 'quickly!'; distinct from 速い, fast

rows.story: Something ten mouths have already told the story of.
rows.wild: 中古 — second-hand

rows.story: A standing tree and an axe. Cut it and the wood is new.
rows.wild: 新聞 — newspaper, literally new hearing

rows.story: Evening after evening. It adds up.
rows.wild: 多分 — probably

topics.blurb: Seasons, landscape and colour. The adjectives here are among the first you will actually use in conversation.
topics.foot: 暑い and 熱い are both atsui. 暑い is the weather; 熱い is the soup.

rows.story: Insects blown sideways past a window frame.
rows.wild: 風邪 — a cold, confusingly written with the same sound

rows.story: Rain you have to sweep.
rows.wild: 大雪 — heavy snow, on weather warnings

rows.story: Every water there is, poured into one place.
rows.wild: 海外 — overseas, literally outside the sea

rows.story: Three trees. Now you cannot.
rows.wild: Three trees; 林 is two

rows.story: Two trees side by side. You can still walk between them.
rows.wild: Common as a surname

rows.story: The open ground the village was laid out on before anyone built anything.
rows.wild: 野 alone is open plain; 野球 is baseball

rows.story: A rock that has come off a cliff.
rows.wild: 石油 — petroleum

parts: kanji + kana · 小さい・ちいさい
rows.story: Small sparks that grew legs and walked off in every direction.
rows.wild: 観光 — sightseeing, literally looking at the light

rows.story: A bird's mouth. It also covers phones ringing.
rows.wild: Also 鳴く, the sound an animal makes

parts: radical · a roof with walls, on top
rows.story: Straw stuffed under the roof and ice underneath anyway.
rows.wild: 寒気 — a chill

rows.story: Sun directly on a person, with nowhere to go.
rows.wild: Distinct from 熱い, hot to the touch

rows.story: Water going further down than you can see.
rows.wild: 深夜 — the small hours

rows.story: New growth under moonlight, which is neither blue nor green but both.
rows.wild: Also covers green traffic lights

rows.story: Earth with a fire under it, glowing.
rows.wild: 赤ちゃん — baby

rows.story: A village burnt down. What is left is black.
rows.wild: 黒板 — blackboard

topics.blurb: Signage kanji. You will read these off a street sign or a station exit long before you write them.
topics.foot: On a station board, 発 is departures and 着 is arrivals. Two kanji, and you can read the timetable.

rows.story: Fields nailed down into blocks. That is a town.
rows.wild: Half of all Japanese addresses contain it

parts: radical · a box on its side
rows.story: A box with a cross cut through it: the city carved into wards.
rows.wild: Tokyo is divided into 23 区

rows.story: Cloth hung under an awning. A market, and then a city.
rows.wild: 市役所 — city hall

rows.story: An administrative eye kept on a region.
rows.wild: The administrative level above 市

parts: kanji + kana · 食べる・たべる
rows.story: An official building where they feed you. Libraries and embassies both.
rows.wild: 美術館, 大使館, 映画館 — 館 is any large public building

rows.story: Ground with the sun on it. Somewhere you can actually point to.
rows.wild: 会場 — venue; 工場 — factory

rows.story: Land measured out and set aside. That is what a temple is.

rows.story: Where one field stops and the next begins, extended until it means the world.
rows.wild: 業界 — an industry

rows.story: Two hands lifting the bar out of the gate.

topics.blurb: The kanji that do not belong to a place or a scene, but turn up constantly in compounds.
topics.foot: 以上 and 以下 appear on almost every Japanese form, sign and price bracket. Learn the pair now.

rows.story: A kneeling figure with a marked face. Colour and complexion.
rows.wild: 景色 — scenery, an irregular reading

rows.story: Two lines over a pair of legs: where a person starts from.
rows.wild: 元 alone means the origin or former state

rows.story: The grain in a jewel, which tells you how it will split. Its underlying logic.

rows.story: Everything under the king's roof, without exception.
rows.wild: 安全 — safety, literally wholly at ease

apx.name: kanji
apx.note: Real kanji that work as words on their own. Every one of these is a free extra character.

apx.name: kanji + kana
apx.note: Real kanji, but they only become words with a hiragana tail. Learn the kanji and its okurigana together — the tail is part of the word.

apx.name: compounds only
apx.note: Real kanji you will not meet standing alone. Learn them as parts of the compounds shown.

apx.name: radical
apx.note: Not kanji. Positional shapes with no reading and no independent use. Recognise them so the breakdowns make sense; never try to learn them as characters.

apx.name: rare
apx.note: Genuine kanji, but far beyond N4. Treat them as scaffolding inside the character you are actually learning.

lede: The same stories as the shape deck, resorted by where you will actually use them: the restaurant, the bar, the pharmacy, the station, the office. Within each topic, kanji are grouped by whether their anchor word is a noun, a verb or an adjective.
Every entry carries a real word rather than an abstract keyword, and a line saying where in Japan you will actually run into it — on a menu, a departure board, a shop curtain, a clinic door.
